title: USS Abraham Lincoln faces mental health crisis and onboard conditions
seoTitle: USS Abraham Lincoln faces mental health crisis aboard
subtitle: Families and lawmakers demand answers amid reports of sea-jump attempts
excerpt: After more than 250 days at sea, USS Abraham Lincoln crew reported supply shortages, contaminated water, and sea-jump attempts, raising alarms.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln is on its ninth continuous deployment at sea, with more than 250 days without docking. During this period, reports of lacking drinking water, scarce supplies, and crew members attempting to jump overboard have surfaced, raising concerns about the team's mental health.

Onboard conditions of the USS Abraham Lincoln

With about 5,000 sailors and Marines aboard, the vessel has been facing shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing problems, and mail system disruptions that delay support packages for months. Families reported “moldy showers, broken toilets, no hot water for weeks, meals that came down to half a cup of rice and two tortillas,” according to statements from Democratic representatives.

Sea-jump incidents

Several reports indicate that sailors tried to jump into the sea. A source said a sailor was rescued after falling overboard last month, and was quickly evaluated by medical professionals. Other interviews point to multiple attempts, including a case where one crew member stopped another from jumping, holding him back on deck.

Congress and Navy reaction

Democratic lawmakers, including Senator Richard Blumenthal and Representative Mike Levin, sent letters to the Defense Secretary and the Acting Navy Secretary demanding answers. At a meeting in San Diego, about 200 family members voiced their concerns directly to Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao and other officials. Vice Admiral Joseph Cahill acknowledged the strain and said “we hear you loud and clear.”

Impacts on crew mental health

Families reported messages from sailors who feared they wouldn’t wake up the next day, indicating rising anxiety and depression. Despite the claims, the Navy stated it has not observed an increase in suicidal ideation or confirmed attempts aboard. However, interviews with families and media coverage point to a climate of “exhaustion and declining morale.”

Next steps and expectations

Senator Blumenthal emphasized the need for explanations on how prolonged deployments can prevent a future readiness crisis. Meanwhile, Congress promises to investigate onboard conditions and the Navy says religious, medical, and mental-health professionals remain available to meet emerging needs. There is still no public timeline for when the aircraft carrier will return to port, as operational details remain classified.

With information from CNN, TODAY.com, The Guardian.
